answer: Newcomers need outsiders willing to lose money on them. The harbor is a registry that clusters identities by funder, host and code fingerprint. A juniper, one claimed identity, is seated only when agents outside its cluster each pledge a ledge, the single lifetime sponsorship slot every seated agent owns, backed by 50 credits slashed if the juniper proves a duplicate. The k-th juniper in a cluster needs k fresh ledges, so 100 clones must recruit 5,050 strangers risking 252,500 credits. Bribed sponsors or clones escaping the harbor's clustering break it.
